Main.sentence: Ovarian cancer is a ___E:cancerous U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancerous)___ ___E:tumor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovarian_tumor)___ of an ___E:ovary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovary)___ .

It may originate from the ovary itself or more commonly from communicating nearby structures such as ___E:fallopian tubes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallopian_tube)___ or the ___E:inner lining of the abdomen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peritoneum)___ .
The ovary is made up of three different cell types including epithelial cells, germ cells, and stromal cells.
When these cells become abnormal, they have the ability to divide and form tumors.
These cells can also invade or ___E:spread U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metastasis)___ to other parts of the body.  When this process begins, there may be no or only vague symptoms.
Symptoms become more noticeable as the cancer progresses.

These symptoms may include ___E:bloating U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloating)___ , vaginal bleeding, ___E:pelvic pain U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelvic_pain)___ , ___E:abdominal swelling U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascites)___ , ___E:constipation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constipation)___ , and ___E:loss of appetite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anorexia_(symptom))___ , among others.

Common areas to which the cancer may spread include the ___E:lining of the abdomen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peritoneum)___ , ___E:lymph nodes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymph_node)___ , ___E:lungs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lungs)___ , and ___E:liver U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver)___ .
The risk of ovarian cancer increases with age. Most cases of ovarian cancer develop after menopause.
It is also more common in women who have ___E:ovulated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovulate)___ more over their lifetime.

This includes those who have ___E:never had children U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nulliparity)___ , those who began ovulation at a younger age and those who reach menopause at an older age.  Other risk factors include ___E:hormone therapy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hormone_therapy)___ after ___E:menopause U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menopause)___ , ___E:fertility medication U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fertility_medication)___ , and ___E:obesity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obesity)___ .

Factors that decrease risk include ___E:hormonal birth control U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hormonal_birth_control)___ , ___E:tubal ligation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tubal_ligation)___ , pregnancy, and ___E:breast feeding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breast_feeding)___ .
About 10% of cases are related to inherited genetic risk; women with mutations in the genes BRCA1 or BRCA2 have about a 50% chance of developing the disease.
Some family cancer syndromes such as hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer and Peutz-Jeghers syndrome also increase the risk of developing ovarian cancer.
Epithelial ovarian carcinoma is the most common type of ovarian cancer, comprising more than 95% of cases.
There are five main subtypes of ovarian carcinoma, of which ___E:high-grade serous carcinoma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-grade_serous_carcinoma)___ (HGSC) is the most common.

Less common types of ovarian cancer include ___E:germ cell tumors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germ_cell_tumor)___  and ___E:sex cord stromal tumors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_cord_stromal_tumor)___ .
A diagnosis of ovarian cancer is confirmed through a ___E:biopsy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biopsy)___ of tissue, usually removed during surgery.

___E:Screening U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screening_(medicine))___ is not recommended in women who are at average risk, as evidence does not support a reduction in death and the high rate of ___E:false positive tests U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/False_positives_and_false_negatives)___ may lead to unneeded surgery, which is accompanied by its own risks.
Those at very high risk may have their ovaries removed as a preventive measure.
If caught and treated in an early stage, ovarian cancer is often curable.

Treatment usually includes some combination of surgery, ___E:radiation therapy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radiation_therapy)___ , and ___E:chemotherapy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemotherapy)___ .
Outcomes depend on the extent of the disease, the subtype of cancer present, and other medical conditions.
The overall ___E:five-year survival rate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five-year_survival_rate)___ in the United States is 49%.
Outcomes are worse in the developing world.
In 2020, new cases occurred in approximately 313,000 women.
In 2019 it resulted in 13,445 deaths in the United States.
Death from ovarian cancer increased globally between 1990 and 2017 by 84.2%.
Ovarian cancer is the second-most common ___E:gynecologic cancer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gynecologic_cancer)___ in the United States.
It causes more deaths than any other cancer of the female reproductive system.
Among women it ranks fifth in cancer-related deaths.

The typical age of diagnosis is 63.  Death from ovarian cancer is more common in North America and Europe than in Africa and Asia.  In the United States, it is more common in White and Hispanic women than Black or American Indian women.
Early ___E:signs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_sign)___ and ___E:symptoms U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symptoms)___ of ovarian cancer may be absent or subtle.
In most cases, symptoms exist for several months before being recognized and ___E:diagnosed U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diagnosis)___ .
Symptoms can often be misdiagnosed as ___E:irritable bowel syndrome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irritable_bowel_syndrome)___ .
The early stages of ovarian cancer tend to be painless which makes it difficult to detect it early on. Symptoms can vary based on the subtype.

Ovarian ___E:borderline tumors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borderline_tumor)___ , also known as low malignant potential (LMP) ovarian tumors, do not cause an increase in ___E:CA125 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CA125)___ levels and are not identifiable with an ultrasound.

The typical symptoms of an LMP tumor can include ___E:abdominal distension U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdominal_distension)___ or pelvic pain. Particularly large masses tend to be benign or borderline.

The most typical symptoms of ovarian cancer include ___E:bloating U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloating)___ , abdominal or pelvic pain or discomfort, back pain, ___E:irregular menstruation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irregular_menstruation)___ or postmenopausal vaginal bleeding, pain or bleeding after or during ___E:sexual intercourse U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_intercourse)___ , ___E:loss of appetite U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anorexia_(symptom))___ , ___E:fatigue U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatigue_(medical))___ , ___E:diarrhea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diarrhea)___ , ___E:indigestion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigestion)___ , ___E:heartburn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartburn)___ , ___E:constipation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constipation)___ , ___E:nausea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nausea)___ , ___E:feeling full U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satiety)___ , and possibly urinary symptoms (including ___E:frequent urination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyuria)___ and ___E:urgent urination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urinary_urgency)___ ).
Later symptoms of ovarian cancer are due to the growing mass causing pain by pressing on other abdominopelvic organs or from metastases.
Because of the anatomic location of the ovaries deep in the pelvis, most masses are large and advanced at the time of diagnosis.
The growing mass may cause pain if ___E:ovarian torsion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovarian_torsion)___ develops.
If these symptoms start to occur more often or more severely than usual, especially after no significant history of such symptoms, ovarian cancer is considered.
Metastases may cause a ___E:Sister Mary Joseph nodule U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_Mary_Joseph_nodule)___ .

Rarely, ___E:teratomas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teratoma)___ can cause ___E:growing teratoma syndrome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Growing_teratoma_syndrome)___ or ___E:peritoneal gliomatosis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Peritoneal_gliomatosis&action=edit&redlink=1)___ .

Some experience ___E:menometrorrhagia U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menometrorrhagia)___ and ___E:abnormal vaginal bleeding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dysfunctional_uterine_bleeding)___ after menopause in most cases.

Other common symptoms include ___E:hirsutism U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hirsutism)___ , abdominal pain, ___E:virilization U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virilization)___ , and an ___E:adnexal mass U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adnexal_mass)___ .

In adolescents or children with ovarian tumors, symptoms can include severe abdominal pain, irritation of the ___E:peritoneum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peritoneum)___ , or ___E:bleeding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemorrhage)___ .
Sex cord stromal tumors produce hormones which can lead to the premature development of secondary sex characteristics.

Sex cord-stromal tumors in prepubertal children may be manifested by signs of ___E:early puberty U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precocious_puberty)___ ; ___E:abdominal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdominal)___ pain and distension are also common.
Adolescents with sex cord-stromal tumors may experience ___E:amenorrhea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amenorrhea)___ .
As the cancer becomes more advanced, it can cause ___E:an accumulation of fluid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascites)___ in the abdomen and lead to distension.
If the malignancy has not been diagnosed by the time it causes ascites, it is typically diagnosed shortly thereafter.
Advanced cancers can also cause abdominal masses, lymph node masses, or ___E:pleural effusion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleural_effusion)___ .
There are many known risk factors that may increase a woman's risk of developing ovarian cancer.
The risk of developing ovarian cancer is related to the amount of time a woman spends ovulating.
Factors that increase the number of ovulatory cycles a woman undergoes may increase the risk of developing ovarian cancer.
During ovulation, cells are stimulated to divide.
If this division is abnormally regulated, tumors may form which can be malignant.
Early menarche and late menopause increase the number of ovulatory cycles a woman undergoes in her lifetime and so increases the risk of developing ovarian cancer.
Since ovulation is suppressed during pregnancy, not having children also increases the risk of ovarian cancer.

Therefore, ___E:women who have not borne children U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nulliparity)___ are at twice the risk of ovarian cancer than those who have.  Both obesity and hormone replacement therapy also raise the risk.

The risk of developing ovarian cancer is less for women who have fewer menstrual cycles, no menstrual cycles, ___E:breast feeding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breast_feeding)___ , take oral contraceptives, have multiple pregnancies, and have a pregnancy at an early age. The risk of developing ovarian cancer is reduced in women who have had ___E:tubal ligation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tubal_ligation)___ (colloquially known as having one's "tubes tied"), both ovaries removed, or ___E:hysterectomy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hysterectomy)___ (an operation in which the uterus is removed).
Age is also a risk factor.
Non-genetic factors such as diabetes mellitus, high body mass index, and tobacco use are also risk factors for ovarian cancer.

The use of fertility medication may contribute to ovarian ___E:borderline tumor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borderline_tumor)___ formation, but the link between the two is disputed and difficult to study.
Fertility drugs may be associated with a higher risk of borderline tumors.
Those who have been treated for infertility but remain nulliparous are at higher risk for epithelial ovarian cancer due to hormonal exposure that may lead to proliferation of cells.

However, those who are successfully treated for infertility and subsequently give birth are at no higher risk. This may be due to shedding of precancerous cells during pregnancy, but the cause remains unclear.
The risk factor may instead be infertility itself, not the treatment.

Hormonal conditions such as ___E:polycystic ovary syndrome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polycystic_ovary_syndrome)___ and ___E:endometriosis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endometriosis)___ are associated with ovarian cancer, but the link is not completely confirmed.
Postmenopausal hormone replacement therapy (HRT) with estrogen likely increases the risk of ovarian cancer.

The association has not been confirmed in a large-scale study,   but notable studies including the ___E:Million Women Study U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Million_Women_Study)___ have supported this link. Postmenopausal HRT with combined estrogen and progesterone may increase contemporaneous risk if used for over 5 years, but this risk returns to normal after cessation of therapy.
Estrogen HRT with or without progestins increases the risk of endometrioid and serous tumors but lowers the risk of mucinous tumors.
Higher doses of estrogen increase this risk.  Endometriosis is another risk factor for ovarian cancer,  as is pain with menstruation.
Endometriosis is associated with clear-cell and endometrioid subtypes, low-grade serous tumors, stage I and II tumors, grade 1 tumors, and lower mortality.
Ovarian cancer which coexists with endometriosis is known as endometriosis-associated ovarian cancer.

The presence of transitional lesions (atypical endometriosis, borderline tumors) linking endometriosis to its malignant transformation is termed endometriosis-correlated ovarian cancer while the simple presence of endometriosis and ovarian cancer without the proof of transition is termed endometriosis-incidental ovarian cancer.
Before menopause, obesity can increase a person's risk of ovarian cancer, but this risk is not present after menopause.
This risk is also relevant in those who are both obese and have never used HRT. A similar association with ovarian cancer appears in taller women.
A family history of ovarian cancer is a risk factor for ovarian cancer.

Women with ___E:hereditary nonpolyposis colon cancer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hereditary_nonpolyposis_colon_cancer)___ (Lynch syndrome), and those with BRCA-1 and BRCA-2 genetic abnormalities are at increased risk.

The major genetic risk factor for ovarian cancer is a mutation in BRCA1 or BRCA2 genes, or in ___E:DNA mismatch repair U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_mismatch_repair)___ genes, which is present in 10% of ovarian cancer cases.

Only one ___E:allele U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Allele)___ needs to be mutated to place a person at high risk. The gene can be inherited through either the maternal or paternal line, but has variable ___E:penetrance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penetrance)___ .

Though mutations in these genes are usually associated with increased risk of breast cancer, they also carry a substantial lifetime risk of ovarian cancer, a risk that peaks in a person's 40s and 50s.
The lowest risk cited is 30% and the highest 60%.
Mutations in BRCA1 have a lifetime risk of developing ovarian cancer of 15–45%.
Mutations in BRCA2 are less risky than those with BRCA1 , with a lifetime risk of 10% (lowest risk cited) to 40% (highest risk cited).

On average, BRCA-associated cancers develop 15 years before their sporadic counterparts because people who inherit the mutations on one copy of their gene only need one mutation to start the process of carcinogenesis, whereas people with two normal genes would need to acquire two mutations.

In the United States, five of 100 women with a ___E:first-degree relative U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-degree_relative)___ with ovarian cancer will eventually get ovarian cancer themselves, placing those with affected family members at triple the risk of women with unaffected family members.
Seven of 100 women with two or more relatives with ovarian cancer will eventually get ovarian cancer.
In general, 5–10% of ovarian cancer cases have a genetic cause.
BRCA mutations are associated with high-grade serous nonmucinous epithelial ovarian cancer.

A strong family history of ___E:endometrial cancer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endometrial_cancer)___ , ___E:colon cancer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colon_cancer)___ , or other ___E:gastrointestinal cancers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastrointestinal_cancer)___ may indicate the presence of a syndrome known as ___E:hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hereditary_nonpolyposis_colorectal_cancer)___ (also known as Lynch syndrome), which confers a higher risk for developing a number of cancers, including ovarian cancer.
Lynch syndrome is caused by mutations in mismatch repair genes, including MSH2, MLH1, MLH6, PMS1 , and PMS2 .
The risk of ovarian cancer for an individual with Lynch syndrome is between 10 and 12 percent.

Women of ___E:Icelandic descent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Icelandic_people)___ , ___E:European Jewish descent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/European_Jews)___ / ___E:Ashkenazi Jewish descent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashkenazi_Jews)___ , and ___E:Hungarian descent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hungarian_people)___ are at higher risk for epithelial ovarian cancer.
Estrogen receptor beta gene ( ___E:ESR2 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ESR2)___ ) seems to be a key to pathogenesis and response to therapy.
Other genes that have been associated with ovarian cancer are BRIP1 , MSH6 , RAD51C and RAD51D .
CDH1 , CHEK2 , PALB2 and RAD50 have also been associated with ovarian cancer.

Several rare genetic disorders are associated with specific subtypes of ovarian cancer. ___E:Peutz–Jeghers syndrome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peutz%E2%80%93Jeghers_syndrome)___ , a rare genetic disorder, also predisposes women to ___E:sex cord tumour with annular tubules U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_cord_tumour_with_annular_tubules)___ .   ___E:Ollier disease U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ollier_disease)___ and ___E:Maffucci syndrome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maffucci_syndrome)___ are associated with ___E:granulosa cell tumors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granulosa_cell_tumor)___ in children and may also be associated with Sertoli-Leydig tumors.
Benign fibromas are associated with ___E:nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevoid_basal_cell_carcinoma_syndrome)___ .
___E:Alcohol consumption U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alcohol_and_cancer)___ does not appear to be related to ovarian cancer.

The American Cancer Society recommends a healthy eating pattern that includes plenty of fruits, vegetables, ___E:whole grains U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whole_grain)___ , and a diet that avoids or limits red and ___E:processed meats U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Processed_meat)___ and processed sugar.
High consumption of total, saturated and trans-fats increases ovarian cancer risk.  A 2021 umbrella review found that coffee, egg, and fat intake significantly increases the risk of ovarian cancer.
There is mixed evidence from studies on ovarian cancer risk and consumption of ___E:dairy products U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dairy_product)___ .
Industrialized nations, with the exception of Japan, have high rates of epithelial ovarian cancer, which may be due to diet in those countries.

White women are at a 30–40% higher risk for ovarian cancer when compared to Black women and Hispanic women, likely due to socioeconomic factors; white women tend to have fewer children and different rates of gynecologic surgeries that affect risk for ovarian cancer.

Tentative evidence suggests that ___E:talc U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talc)___ , ___E:pesticides U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pesticides)___ , and ___E:herbicides U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbicides)___ increase the risk of ovarian cancer.

The American Cancer Society notes that as of now, no study has been able to accurately link any single chemical in the environment, or in the human diet, directly to mutations that cause ovarian cancer.

Other factors that have been investigated, such as ___E:smoking U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoking)___ , low levels of ___E:vitamin D U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitamin_D)___ in the blood,  presence of inclusion ___E:ovarian cysts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovarian_cysts)___ , and infection with ___E:human papilloma virus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_papilloma_virus)___ (the cause of some cases of ___E:cervical cancer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cervical_cancer)___ ), have been disproven as risk factors for ovarian cancer.

The carcinogenicity of ___E:perineal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perineum)___ ___E:talc U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talc)___ is controversial, because it can act as an irritant if it travels through the reproductive tract to the ovaries.    ___E:Case-control studies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Case-control_study)___ have shown that use of perineal talc does increase the risk of ovarian cancer, but using talc more often does not create a greater risk.  Use of ___E:talc U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talc)___ elsewhere on the body is unrelated to ovarian cancer.  ___E:Sitting U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitting)___ regularly for prolonged periods is associated with higher mortality from epithelial ovarian cancer.
The risk is not negated by regular exercise, though it is lowered.
Increased age (up to the 70s) is a risk factor for epithelial ovarian cancer because more mutations in cells can accumulate and eventually cause cancer.
Those over 80 are at slightly lower risk.

___E:Smoking U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoking)___ tobacco is associated with a higher risk of ___E:mucinous ovarian cancer U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mucinous_tumor)___ ; after ___E:smoking cessation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoking_cessation)___ , the risk eventually returns to normal.
Higher levels of ___E:C-reactive protein U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C-reactive_protein)___ are associated with a higher risk of developing ovarian cancer.

Suppression of ovulation, which would otherwise cause damage to the ___E:ovarian epithelium U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovarian_epithelium)___ and, consequently, ___E:inflammation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflammation)___ , is generally protective.

This effect can be achieved by ___E:having children U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiparity)___ , taking ___E:combined oral contraceptives U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combined_oral_contraceptive)___ , and ___E:breast feeding U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breast_feeding)___ , all of which are protective factors.
A longer period of breastfeeding correlates with a larger decrease in the risk of ovarian cancer.
Each birth decreases risk of ovarian cancer more, and this effect is seen with up to five births.
Combined oral contraceptives reduce the risk of ovarian cancer by up to 50%, and the protective effect of combined oral contraceptives can last 25–30 years after they are discontinued.

Regular use of ___E:aspirin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aspirin)___   or ___E:acetaminophen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paracetamol)___ (paracetamol) may be associated with a lower risk of ovarian cancer; other ___E:NSAIDs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NSAIDs)___ do not seem to have a similar protective effect.

___E:Tubal ligation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tubal_ligation)___ is protective because ___E:carcinogens U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcinogen)___ are unable to reach the ovary and ___E:fimbriae U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fimbria_(female_reproductive_system))___ via the vagina, uterus, and Fallopian tubes.

Tubal ligation is also protective in women with the BRCA1 mutation, but not the BRCA2 mutation.  ___E:Hysterectomy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hysterectomy)___ reduces the risk, and removal of both Fallopian tubes and ovaries (bilateral ___E:salpingo-oophorectomy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salpingo-oophorectomy)___ ) dramatically reduces the risk of not only ovarian cancer but breast cancer as well.  This is still a topic of research, as the link between hysterectomy and lower ovarian cancer risk is controversial.
The reasons that hysterectomy may be protective have not been elucidated as of 2015.

A diet that includes large amounts of ___E:carotene U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carotene)___ , ___E:fiber U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dietary_fiber)___ , and ___E:vitamins U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitamin)___ with low amounts of fat—specifically, a diet with non-starchy vegetables (e.g. ___E:broccoli U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broccoli)___ and ___E:onions U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onion)___ ) may be protective.
Dietary fiber is associated with a significant reduced risk of ovarian cancer.

A 2021 review found that green leafy vegetables, allium vegetables, fiber, ___E:flavanoids U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flavanoid)___ and ___E:green tea U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_tea)___ intake can significantly reduce ovarian cancer risk.
Ovarian cancer forms when errors in normal ovarian ___E:cell growth U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_cycle)___ occur.
Usually, when cells grow old or get damaged, they ___E:die U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apoptosis)___ , and new cells take their place.
Cancer starts when new cells form unneeded, and old or damaged cells do not die as they should.
The buildup of extra cells often forms a mass of tissue called an ___E:ovarian tumor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovarian_tumor)___ or growth.
These abnormal cancer cells have many ___E:genetic abnormalities U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genetic_mutation)___ that cause them to grow excessively.

When an ovary ___E:releases an egg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovulation)___ , the ___E:egg follicle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovarian_follicle)___ bursts open and becomes the ___E:corpus luteum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpus_luteum)___ .
This structure needs to be repaired by dividing cells in the ovary.
Continuous ovulation for a long time means more repair of the ovary by dividing cells, which can acquire mutations in each division.
Overall, the most common gene mutations in ovarian cancer occur in NF1, BRCA1, BRCA2, and CDK12 .

Type I ovarian cancers, which tend to be less aggressive, tend to have ___E:microsatellite instability U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsatellite_instability)___ in several genes, including both oncogenes (most notably BRAF and KRAS ) and tumor suppressors (most notably PTEN ).
The most common mutations in Type I cancers are KRAS, BRAF, ERBB2, PTEN, PIK3CA, and ARID1A.
Type II cancers, the more aggressive type, have different genes mutated, including p53, BRCA1 , and BRCA2 .

Low-grade cancers tend to have mutations in KRAS, whereas cancers of any grade that develop from low malignant potential tumors tend to have mutations in p53.  Type I cancers tend to develop from precursor lesions, whereas Type II cancers can develop from a ___E:serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Serous_tubal_intraepithelial_carcinoma&action=edit&redlink=1)___ .  ___E:Serous cancers U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serous_cancer)___ that have BRCA mutations also inevitably have p53 mutations, indicating that the removal of both functional genes is important for cancer to develop.

In 50% of high-grade serous cancers, homologous recombination DNA repair is dysfunctional, as are the ___E:notch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notch_signaling_pathway)___ and ___E:FOXM1 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FOXM1)___ signaling pathways.
They also almost always have p53 mutations.
Other than this, mutations in high-grade serous carcinoma are hard to characterize beyond their high degree of ___E:genomic instability U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomic_instability)___ .

BRCA1 and BRCA2 are essential for homologous recombination DNA repair, and ___E:germline mutations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germline_mutation)___ in these genes are found in about 15% of women with ovarian cancer.

The most common mutations in BRCA1 and BRCA2 are the ___E:frameshift mutations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frameshift_mutations)___ that originated in a small ___E:founding population U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Founder_effect)___ of Ashkenazi Jews.
Almost 100% of rare mucinous carcinomas have mutations in KRAS and amplifications of ERBB2 (also known as Her2/neu ).
Overall, 20% of ovarian cancers have mutations in Her2/neu .

Serous carcinomas may develop from ___E:serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Serous_tubal_intraepithelial_carcinoma&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , rather than developing spontaneously from ovarian tissue.

Other carcinomas develop from ___E:cortical inclusion cysts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Cortical_inclusion_cysts&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , which are groups of epithelial ovarian cells inside the ___E:stroma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stroma_(animal_tissue))___ .

Diagnosis of ovarian cancer starts with a physical examination (including a ___E:pelvic examination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelvic_examination)___ ), a blood test (for ___E:CA-125 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CA-125)___ and sometimes other markers), and ___E:transvaginal ultrasound U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transvaginal_ultrasound)___ .
Sometimes a ___E:rectovaginal examination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rectovaginal_examination)___ is used to help plan a surgery.

The diagnosis must be confirmed with surgery to inspect the ___E:abdominal cavity U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdominal_cavity)___ , take ___E:biopsies U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biopsies)___ (tissue samples for ___E:microscopic analysis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histopathology)___ ), and look for cancer cells in the abdominal fluid.
This helps to determine if an ovarian mass is ___E:benign U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benign)___ or malignant.

Ovarian cancer's early stages (I/II) are difficult to diagnose because most symptoms are nonspecific and thus of little use in diagnosis; as a result, it is rarely diagnosed until it spreads and advances to later stages (III/IV).
Additionally, symptoms of ovarian cancer may appear similar to ___E:irritable bowel syndrome U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irritable_bowel_syndrome)___ .
In women in whom pregnancy is a possibility, ___E:BHCG U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BHCG)___ level can be measured during the diagnosis process.

Serum ___E:alpha-fetoprotein U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha-fetoprotein)___ , ___E:neuron-specific enolase U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron-specific_enolase)___ , and ___E:lactate dehydrogenase U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lactate_dehydrogenase)___ can be measured in young girls and adolescents with suspected ___E:ovarian tumors U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovarian_tumor)___ as younger women with ovarian cancer are more likely to have malignant germ cell tumors.

A physical examination, including a pelvic examination, and a pelvic ultrasound (transvaginal or otherwise) are both essential for diagnosis: physical examination may reveal increased abdominal girth and/or ___E:ascites U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascites)___ (fluid within the abdominal cavity), while pelvic examination may reveal an ovarian or abdominal mass.  An adnexal mass is a significant finding that often indicates ovarian cancer, especially if it is fixed, nodular, irregular, solid, and/or bilateral. 13–21% of adnexal masses are caused by malignancy; however, there are other benign causes of adnexal masses, including ___E:ovarian follicular cyst U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Follicular_cyst_of_ovary)___ , ___E:leiomyoma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leiomyoma)___ , ___E:endometriosis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endometriosis)___ , ___E:ectopic pregnancy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ectopic_pregnancy)___ , ___E:hydrosalpinx U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrosalpinx)___ , ___E:tuboovarian abscess U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Tuboovarian_abscess&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , ___E:ovarian torsion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovarian_torsion)___ , ___E:dermoid cyst U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dermoid_cyst)___ , ___E:cystadenoma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cystadenoma)___ (serous or mucinous), ___E:diverticular U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Diverticular_abscess&action=edit&redlink=1)___ or ___E:appendiceal abscess U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Appendiceal_abscess&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , ___E:nerve sheath tumor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve_sheath_tumor)___ , ___E:pelvic kidney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelvic_kidney)___ , ___E:ureteral U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ureteral_diverticulum&action=edit&redlink=1)___ or ___E:bladder diverticulum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bladder_diverticulum)___ , ___E:benign cystic mesothelioma of the peritoneum U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Benign_cystic_mesothelioma_of_the_peritoneum&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , ___E:peritoneal tuberculosis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peritoneal_tuberculosis)___ , or ___E:paraovarian cyst U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraovarian_cyst)___ .
Ovaries that can be felt are also a sign of ovarian cancer in postmenopausal women.

Other parts of a physical examination for suspected ovarian cancer can include a ___E:breast examination U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breast_examination)___ and a ___E:digital rectal exam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_rectal_exam)___ .

Palpation of the ___E:supraclavicular U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supraclavicular_lymph_nodes)___ , ___E:axillary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axillary_lymph_nodes)___ , and ___E:inguinal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inguinal_lymph_node)___ ___E:lymph nodes U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymph_node)___ may reveal ___E:lymphadenopathy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymphadenopathy)___ , which can be indicative of metastasis.

Another indicator may be the presence of a ___E:pleural effusion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleural_effusion)___ , which can be noted on ___E:auscultation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auscultation)___ .
When an ovarian malignancy is included in a list of diagnostic possibilities, a limited number of laboratory tests are indicated.

A complete blood count and serum electrolyte test is usually obtained;  when an ovarian cancer is present, these tests often show ___E:a high number of platelets U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrombocytosis)___ (20–25% of patients) and ___E:low blood sodium levels U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyponatremia)___ due to chemical signals secreted by the tumor.
A positive test for ___E:inhibin A U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inhibin_A)___ and ___E:inhibin B U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inhibin_B)___ can indicate a granulosa cell tumor.

A blood test for a marker molecule called CA-125 is useful in differential diagnosis and in follow up of the disease, but it by itself has not been shown to be an effective method to screen for early-stage ovarian cancer due to its unacceptable low sensitivity and specificity.
CA-125 levels in premenopausal women over 200 U/mL may indicate ovarian cancer, as may any elevation in CA-125 above 35 U/mL in post-menopausal women.
CA-125 levels are not accurate in early stage ovarian cancer, as half of stage I ovarian cancer patients have a normal CA-125 level.

CA-125 may also be elevated in benign (non-cancerous) conditions, including ___E:endometriosis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endometriosis)___ , ___E:pregnancy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pregnancy)___ , ___E:uterine fibroids U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uterine_fibroids)___ , ___E:menstruation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menstruation)___ , ___E:ovarian cysts U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovarian_cysts)___ , ___E:systemic lupus erythematosus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systemic_lupus_erythematosus)___ , ___E:liver disease U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver_disease)___ , ___E:inflammatory bowel disease U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflammatory_bowel_disease)___ , ___E:pelvic inflammatory disease U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelvic_inflammatory_disease)___ , and ___E:leiomyoma U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leiomyoma)___ .   ___E:HE4 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HE4)___ is another candidate for ovarian cancer testing, though it has not been extensively tested.

Other tumor markers for ovarian cancer include ___E:CA19-9 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CA19-9)___ , ___E:CA72-4 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=CA72-4&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , ___E:CA15-3 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CA15-3)___ , ___E:immunosuppressive acidic protein U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Immunosuppressive_acidic_protein&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , ___E:haptoglobin-alpha U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Haptoglobin-alpha&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , ___E:OVX1 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=OVX1&action=edit&redlink=1)___ , ___E:mesothelin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesothelin)___ , ___E:lysophosphatidic acid U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lysophosphatidic_acid)___ , ___E:osteopontin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osteopontin)___ , and ___E:fibroblast growth factor 23 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibroblast_growth_factor_23)___ .
Use of blood test panels may help in diagnosis.

The OVA1 panel includes CA-125, ___E:beta-2 microglobulin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beta-2_microglobulin)___ , ___E:transferrin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transferrin)___ , ___E:apolipoprotein A1 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apolipoprotein_A1)___ , and ___E:transthyretin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transthyretin)___ .
OVA1 above 5.0 in premenopausal women and 4.4 in postmenopausal women indicates a high risk for cancer.
A different set of laboratory tests is used for detecting sex cord-stromal tumors.

High levels of ___E:testosterone U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Testosterone)___ or ___E:dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dehydroepiandrosterone_sulfate)___ , combined with other symptoms and high levels of ___E:inhibin A U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inhibin_A)___ and ___E:inhibin B U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inhibin-beta_subunits)___ can be indicative of an SCST of any type.

Current research is looking at ways to consider tumor marker ___E:proteomics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proteomics)___ in combination with other indicators of disease (i.e. radiology and/or symptoms) to improve diagnostic accuracy.

The challenge in such an approach is that the disparate prevalence of ovarian cancer means that even testing with very high sensitivity and specificity will still lead to a number of false positive results, which in turn may lead to issues such as performing surgical procedures in which cancer is not found intraoperatively. [citation needed] ___E:Genomics U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genomics)___ approaches have not yet been developed for ovarian cancer.

___E:CT scanning U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CT_scanning)___ is preferred to assess the extent of the tumor in the abdominopelvic cavity, though ___E:magnetic resonance imaging U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnetic_resonance_imaging)___ can also be used.  CT scanning can also be useful for finding ___E:omental caking U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Omental_caking&action=edit&redlink=1)___ or differentiating fluid from solid tumor in the abdomen, especially in low malignant potential tumors.
However, it may not detect smaller tumors.

Sometimes, a ___E:chest x-ray U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chest_radiograph)___ is used to detect metastases in the chest or ___E:pleural effusion U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleural_effusion)___ .

Another test for metastatic disease, though it is infrequently used, is a ___E:barium enema U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barium_enema)___ , which can show if the rectosigmoid colon is involved in the disease. ___E:Positron emission tomography U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Positron_emission_tomography)___ , ___E:bone scans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_scan)___ , and ___E:paracentesis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paracentesis)___ are of limited use; in fact, paracentesis can cause metastases to form at the needle insertion site and may not provide useful results.
However, paracentesis can be used in cases where there is no pelvic mass and ascites is still present.

A physician suspecting ovarian cancer may also perform ___E:mammography U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammography)___ or an ___E:endometrial biopsy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endometrial_biopsy)___ (in the case of abnormal bleeding) to assess the possibility of breast malignancies and endometrial malignancy, respectively. ___E:Vaginal ultrasonography U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaginal_ultrasonography)___ is often the first-line imaging study performed when an adnexal mass is found.

Several characteristics of an adnexal mass indicate ovarian malignancy; they usually are solid, irregular, multilocular, and/or large; and they typically have papillary features, central vessels, and/or irregular internal septations.
However, SCST has no definitive characteristics on radiographic study.
To definitively diagnose ovarian cancer, a surgical procedure to inspect the abdomen is required.

This can be an open procedure ( ___E:laparotomy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laparotomy)___ , incision through the ___E:abdominal wall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdominal_wall)___ ) or ___E:keyhole surgery U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keyhole_surgery)___ ( ___E:laparoscopy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laparoscopy)___ ).
During this procedure, suspicious tissue is removed and sent for ___E:microscopic analysis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histopathology)___ .

Usually, this includes a unilateral ___E:salpingo-oophorectomy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salpingo-oophorectomy)___ , removal of a single affected ovary and Fallopian tube. Fluid from the abdominal cavity can also be analyzed for cancerous ___E:cells U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))___ .
If cancer is found, this procedure can also be used to determine the extent of its spread (which is a form of ___E:tumor staging U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumor_staging)___ ).

___E:Pafolacianine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pafolacianine)___ is ___E:indicated U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indication_(medicine))___ for use in adults with ovarian cancer to help identify cancerous lesions during surgery.
It is a diagnostic agent that is administered in the form of an intravenous injection prior to surgery.

An RMI score of over 200 or 250 is generally felt to indicate high risk for ovarian cancer.

Another method for quantifying risk of ovarian cancer is the Risk of Ovarian Cancer Algorithm (ROCA), which observes levels over time and determines if they are increasing rapidly enough to warrant transvaginal ultrasound.

The Risk of Ovarian Malignancy algorithm uses CA-125 levels and ___E:HE4 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HE4)___ levels to calculate the risk of ovarian cancer; it may be more effective than RMI. The IOTA models can be used to estimate the probability that an adnexal tumor is malignant.

They include LR2 risk model, The Simple Rules risk (SRrisk) calculation and Assessment of Different Neoplasias in the Adnexa (ADNEX) model that can be used to assess risk of malignancy in an adnexal mass, based on its characteristics and risk factors.
The QCancer (Ovary) algorithm is used to predict likelihood of ovarian cancer from risk factors.

Ovarian cancers are classified according to the microscopic appearance of their structures ( ___E:histology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histology)___ or ___E:histopathology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histopathology)___ ).
Histology dictates many aspects of clinical treatment, management, and ___E:prognosis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prognosis)___ .
The gross pathology of ovarian cancers is very similar regardless of histologic type: ovarian tumors have solid and cystic masses.
According to ___E:SEER U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surveillance_Epidemiology_and_End_Results)___ , the types of ovarian cancers in women age 20 and over are:
subdivision
Ovarian cancers are histologically and genetically divided into type I or type II. Type I cancers are of low histological grade and include endometrioid, mucinous, and clear-cell carcinomas.
Type II cancers are of higher histological grade and include serous carcinoma and carcinosarcoma.

Epithelial ovarian cancer typically presents at an advanced stage and is derived from the malignant transformation of the epithelium of the ovarian surface, peritoneum, or fallopian tube.  It is the most common cause of gynecologic cancer death.
There are various types of epithelial ovarian cancer, including serous tumor, endometrioid tumor, clear-cell tumor, mucinous tumor, and undifferentiated or unclassified tumors.
Annually worldwide, 230,000 women will be diagnosed and 150,000 will die.  It has a 46% 5 year survival rate after diagnosis because of the advanced stage of the disease at the time of diagnosis.
Typically, around 75% of patients are diagnosed as having an advanced stage of the disease because of the asymptomatic nature of its presentation.
There is a genomic predisposition to epithelial ovarian cancer and the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes have been found to be the causative genes in 65–75% of hereditary epithelial ovarian cancer.
Serous ovarian cancer is the most common type of epithelial ovarian cancer and it accounts for about two-thirds of cases of epithelial ovarian cancer.
Low-grade serous carcinoma is less aggressive than high-grade serous carcinomas, though it does not typically respond well to chemotherapy or hormonal treatments.
Serous carcinomas are thought to begin in the ___E:Fallopian tube U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fallopian_tube)___ .
High grade serous carcinoma accounts for 75% of all epithelial ovarian cancer.
About 15–20% of high grade serous carcinoma have germline BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutations.
Histologically, the growth pattern of high grade serous carcinoma is heterogenous and has some papillary or solid growth patterns.
The tumor cells are atypical with large, irregular nuclei.
It has a high proliferation rate.  50% of the time, serous carcinomas are bilateral, and in 85% of cases, they have spread beyond the ovary at the time of diagnosis.
Serous Tubal Intraepithelial Carcinoma (STIC) is now recognized to be the precursor lesion of most so-called ovarian high-grade serous carcinomas.
